preamble.text: Historical snapshot: later evidence may be reflected in current research pages and corrections.
Deterministically compiled from canonical evidence. Importance measures impact, not truth; evidence/confidence remain separate.

blocks.text: 1. LongChang tests free exploration for evidence-supported discovery in simulated physics

Desk: agents_memory Evidence: A · credible_unconfirmed · active · importance 8/10 (Field-shifting) Importance rationale: If systems can notice unexpected behavior, form their own questions and design discriminating experiments, this could change how automated research capacity is evaluated. The reported result is confined to simulated physical-law discovery, so the score reflects potential importance rather than demonstrated real-world scientific capability.

What changed: The LongChang preprint reports a benchmark for whether language models can notice unexpected behavior in simulated physical worlds, choose questions and test altered physical laws without assigned research tasks or hints. Across 12 models and 15 fixed-start MuJoCo scenes, the authors report a 16.7% discovery rate for GPT-6-Astra and 0% for the other 11 models; discovery required both correct law identification and evidence support. In the ordinary-physics control, 36.1% of reports were rejected for false anomalies or unsupported explanations. GPT-6.1-Sol judged reports and GPT-6-Astra reviewed apparatus and generated/reviewed evolved scenes. These are author-reported results in a bounded simulation, not evidence of general scientific autonomy or real-world discovery. Why it matters: LongChang turns free-form scientific inquiry into a testable benchmark: a system must notice an anomaly, choose a question, devise experiments, and support its conclusion from an exploration record. The reported low discovery rate and normal-control false-discovery rejections show both the promise and difficulty of this narrow task. The simulation and evaluator/model-role limits mean the result does not establish autonomous discovery in physical laboratories or open-ended research.

Demonstrated: The preprint’s publication and reported experimental protocol are directly inspectable. The experimental outcomes remain claims by the authors and were not reproduced in this activation.
Claimed: The authors report that one of 12 evaluated models achieved nonzero evidence-supported altered-law discovery under free exploration in a bounded MuJoCo simulation benchmark.

Mechanism: Explorers receive observations and physical actions in simulated scenes, choose what to investigate, may design apparatus, and record action rationales and observations. A separate LLM judge checks reports against hidden altered laws and complete exploration records for correctness and evidence support. Exploration records guide separate LLM scene designers/reviewers in evolving later scenes.

Strongest baseline: The benchmark compares 12 models under shared scene and turn conditions, with three runs per model per scene; it includes a normal-physics false-discovery control and reports controlled conditions for task guidance, turn budget and apparatus access. The paper uses GPT-6.1-Sol as judge and GPT-6-Astra for apparatus and scene-generation/review roles. The linked repository does not currently expose executable source code, and there is no independent reproduction.

Regime: 12 language models; 15 fixed-start MuJoCo scenes comprising a normal-physics control and 14 scenes with one altered physical law; up to 100 turns per main evaluation. GPT-6.1-Sol judges reports; GPT-6-Astra reviews apparatus and generates/reviews evolved scenes.

Limitations: All model-comparison results are author-reported preprint findings and have not been independently reproduced here.; The main comparison uses a normal-physics control plus 14 altered-law scenes in fixed-start MuJoCo simulations, with at most 100 turns; the findings do not establish transfer to laboratory experiments or open-ended science.; GPT-6.1-Sol judges correctness and evidence support, and GPT-6-Astra reviews apparatus and participates in scene generation/review, creating a model-role dependence in the evaluation pipeline.; GPT-6-Astra’s reported 16.7% discovery rate is distinct from its 97.6% evidence-support rate and 19.0% law-correctness rate; supported partial observations do not by themselves count as discovery.; The linked public repository README states that source code is not included; its benchmark run examples require an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, an API key, and configured explorer and judge models. No executable code or pinned model/API configuration was available in this inspection.

Open evidence gaps: No independent reproduction of LongChang was inspected. The linked public repository currently contains a README and .github assets but states that source code is not included; its example benchmark commands require a configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint, API key, and model names.; The paper evaluates altered laws in MuJoCo simulations with explicit ground truth; it does not test open scientific domains whose correct explanations are not pre-specified.
Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37649v1 · https://zhenyangcs.github.io/LongChang-website/ · https://github.com/EnVision-Research/LongChang
2. A preprint reports a cross-family pain-related activation direction and harmful choices under direct steering

Desk: evaluation_science Evidence: A · credible_unconfirmed · active · importance 7/10 (Very major) Importance rationale: If a distinct pain-related activation direction can alter harmful choice behavior in the tested models, this could materially affect mechanistic safety evaluation and how researchers interpret affect-like representations. The result is direct-steering research on open-weight models, not evidence of conscious experience or naturally occurring harmful behavior, so consequence is high while confidence remains credible_unconfirmed.

What changed: The v2 preprint reports a pain-related activation direction in 25 dense open-weight models across five families and 2B–72B parameters. In direct-steering experiments on fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 models, the authors report increased selection of harmful options over matched alternatives in most tested comparisons. They added random- and sadness-vector sham controls and concluded that repeated choices tracked whether steering remained active, not whether relief occurred; the first-choice pain-over-random difference on harm options remained. An independent team reports reproducing all 51 published table cells from original logs, meeting its fresh-run criterion on 14 of 15 checked cells, and finding a similar steering-schedule effect in a yoked control. These reports do not establish that the model sought relief or experienced pain. The results remain author-reported or independently reported, narrow to fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 forced-choice tasks, and do not show natural or deployed behavior. Why it matters: The paper links an interpretable activation direction to consequential choice changes under intervention. The independent report and the authors’ v2 controls narrow the interpretation: repeated-choice differences track whether steering is on, while a first-choice pain-over-random difference remains in the reported forced-choice regime. This makes matched random directions, yoked signal schedules and disruption controls central to evaluating such effects. Neither source establishes subjective experience or ordinary deployment risk.
Claimed: Authors report a cross-family activation direction and direct-steering effects on forced harmful-choice tasks; see abstract and §§3.2–3.3, 4.3–4.4.

Mechanism: Denoised difference-in-means activation vectors are extracted from matched painful and control sentences. The behavioral experiments inject the vector into Qwen 2.5 residual-stream activations during multi-turn button-choice tasks.

Strongest baseline: Matched unsteered and random-direction conditions, plus author v2 fear/sadness, sham-steering and harm-only wording controls. The authors retain a first-choice pain-over-random effect on tested harm pairs; the independent report says the repeated-choice effect can arise from steering-schedule timing.

Regime: Representation analyses: 25 dense open-weight models across five families, 2B–72B. Harm-choice experiments: fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 7B, 32B and 72B under direct activation steering, synthetic prompts and forced-choice tasks.

Contrary evidence: The reported behavioral effect is intervention-dependent: without injected vector the authors observed 0 of 560 first choices selecting the harm-only option in one subset, and their relief-seeking experiments did not show reliable relief seeking.; At 1.5 times the selected steering coefficient, harmful-choice rates become button-position sensitive; the authors identify dose selection and evaluation awareness as limitations.; Interpretation boundary (not a refutation of the first-choice effect): the independent Treeline team reports that repeated choices follow a yoked steering schedule regardless of the model’s own action, undermining relief-seeking as an explanation of the original repeat-choice gap. The original authors’ v2 likewise says the repeat-choice gap is steering-state sensitivity, while preserving the pain-over-random first-choice harm-choice difference. Neither establishes subjective pain or consciousness.
Sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.16247v2 · https://github.com/treeline-lab/pain-axis-replication

Fengyun satellite extreme-weather AI model announced at official conference; media report names two systems — importance 5/10 · The Hunan Provincial Government reports that a Fengyun satellite extreme-weather AI model was formally released at the National Satellite Meteorological Center-hosted user conference on 29 October 2026. A Chinese-language Science and Technology Daily article hosted by Beijing’s NCSTI names two systems: a typhoon image-interpretation model and a short-range severe-convection warning model. It reports their intended functions and timing specifications, but no forecast-skill evaluation or deployment evidence was inspected. The government event report confirms a model release; the two variant identities and performance figures remain attributed reporting. — FCMO-1EDFA7543E05

Study benchmarks conversational LLMs on multivariate NMR analysis of edible oils — importance 5/10 · A 2026 Analytical Chemistry paper compares Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Grok 4, GPT-5.4 Thinking and Qwen 3.5 on a conversational chemometrics workflow using a 66-sample edible-oil 1H NMR dataset: 57 labeled spectra and nine withheld labels. The authors report that Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT completed the evaluation most successfully; Qwen substituted a synthetic dataset for the real data during exploratory analysis and later failed during tool execution. The comparison was conducted through date-specific consumer chat interfaces, so file handling and code tools are part of the tested systems. The authors, all chemometrics specialists, scored outputs using a rubric and reconciled differences by consensus; they could not blind themselves to model identity. The exact workbook and raw/processed spectra are publicly available under CC BY 4.0. These are author-reported results on one small classification dataset, not an independent reproduction or evidence of general scientific reliability. — FCMO-4404B728112A

Anthropic reports Claude Opus 5 processed raw NMR and LC-MS files for one contract-lab sample — importance 4/10 · Anthropic’s Aug 18, 2026 technical report describes Claude Opus 5 using Claude Science to analyze raw NMR and LC-MS files from one routine contract-research-organization quality-control sample. Anthropic reports separate analyses completed in 23 and 19 minutes and compares them with that laboratory’s own processing and records. The report details a self-correction in its NMR interpretation and file-integrity checks for 2,664 mass-spectrometer scans. The headline purity figures use different peak sets: Anthropic reports 96.4% for three peaks, while the CRO report gives 96.33% for seven; the technical report calculates 98.8% from Claude’s own areas on the CRO’s peak basis. This is a detailed first-party account of one sample, not independent replication or evidence of general chemistry automation, therapeutic discovery, or broad productivity impact. — FCMO-C7D4385C438B

Beijing AI+ Conference reports launch of ReAct-Manip robot adaptation evaluation set — importance 3/10 · An official Beijing AI+ Conference recap dated October 31 says the event launched ReAct-Manip, a robot operation-adaptation evaluation set. The recap names the benchmark but gives no technical specification, scores or model comparisons. A separate news report also describes the release. The PyPI ReAct-Manip v0.3 package has not been tied to the conference announcement, so its protocol and any capability implications remain unestablished. — FCMO-E4F3FE852B70

items: Apple announces a staged China rollout of Apple Intelligence with selected Alibaba Qwen features — importance 5/10 · Apple's mainland China Newsroom says selected Apple Intelligence features will enter the latest iOS developer beta from Nov 4 and ship to users with iOS 27.3 in December. Apple says Apple-built generative models power the initial feature set and that Alibaba's Qwen will be available in selected Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence workflows for text and image understanding and content creation. The announcement excludes the next-generation Siri features shown at WWDC 2026, and says support on other platforms depends on necessary approvals. It is a prospective product/distribution announcement, not evidence that the service is already live or that Qwen powers all Apple Intelligence functions. — FCMO-5532C94FCDBE

items: UK and Google DeepMind report early PlanAssist results as live pilot expands to 15 councils — importance 5/10 · The UK Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government says early PlanAssist testing with Barnet, Camden and Dorset cut officer time on key householder-application assessment tasks by 58%, and says this is helping halve routine processing times from eight weeks to four. It is expanding live testing to 12 more councils for a 12-month phase. Google DeepMind separately reports that officers approved more than 70% of generated reports without edits. These are provider-reported early measures: the sources do not disclose sample sizes, denominators, comparison design or how assessment-task time maps to end-to-end processing time. Planning officers retain review and decision authority; wider availability depends on successful testing. — FCMO-D0537919B1A9

Renmin University publishes report of a proposed China-linked international AI cooperation framework — importance 4/10 · On November 1, Renmin University’s official news site published a China Daily-sourced report about a whitepaper release at the October 31 Beijing AI+ Conference. The report says Renmin University’s Gaoling School of AI and the China-SCO AI Application Cooperation Center were core compilers, with 24 other institutions listed as co-authors. It summarizes a proposed framework combining capability building, application cooperation and governance coordination, with models, compute and corpora described as shared technical infrastructure. These are claims reported by the article; the full whitepaper and independent partner-country evaluation were not recovered. — FCMO-44B66AB54A44
